result.title: PopGen: Generating Semantically Diverse Populations for Zero-Shot Coordination
result.summary: In multi-agent reinforcement learning, exposing a cooperator to partners with diverse strategies during training is key to better collaboration at test time. However, existing methods typically rely on trajectory-level proxies to measure diversity, which may label two distinct trajectories of the same strategy as diverse. Instead, our key insight is to leverage LLMs' ability to describe behaviorally distinct agents in environments, similar to how humans can recognize high-level strategies. To this end, we introduce PopGen, a framework that synthesizes semantically diverse agents from scratch using LLMs. PopGen first generates a diverse set of textual descriptions of agent behaviors, then translates each behavior into a code policy that can be executed within the environment. We show that cooperators trained against PopGen populations achieve robust zero-shot cooperation with unseen partners, outperforming population-play baselines across four collaborative environments. We further show that semantic diversity scales with PopGen population size, improving the cooperator's worst-case performance, and we identify design choices that preserve population quality while maximizing diversity. Our code is available at https://github.com/labicon/PopGen.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 PopGen，用 LLM 从零生成多样化的智能体行为文本描述并转译为可执行策略代码，以此构建多智能体强化学习的训练种群，使合作者能对未见伙伴实现更稳健的零样本协作，并在四个协作环境中超过 population-play 基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以语义描述而非轨迹级代理来度量行为多样性」的思路，可能为 LVR 中区分 latent 相似度的实质内容与表层差异、以及训练分布多样性如何影响长度与任务泛化提供可核查的启发；但论文属多智能体协作领域，无视觉或 latent 推理状态，联系较间接。
